1: # NEX Arm · 3-Camera Eval
2: 
3: Browser frontend that shows the three robot cameras side by side and **never opens the built-in FaceTime camera**.
4: 
5: | Tile | Device (as macOS reports it) | USB VID:PID |
6: |---|---|---|
7: | Robot Wrist (USB) | `icspring camera` | `32e6:9005` |
8: | RealSense D415 (RGB) | `Intel(R) RealSense(TM) Depth Camera 415 RGB` | `8086:0ad3` |
9: | Logitech C922 | `C922 Pro Stream Webcam` | `046d:085c` |
10: 
11: ## Run
12: 
13: ```bash
14: ./start.sh          # serves on http://localhost:8770 and opens it (PORT=xxxx to change)
15: ```
16: 
17: Use Chrome (recommended) and allow camera access when asked.
18: 
19: ## Features
20: - Finds each camera by name or USB ID; drop-downs let you reassign one by hand
21: - FaceTime / built-in cameras are filtered out of every list
22: - Global resolution (480p / 720p / 1080p) and FPS
23: - Live resolution + measured FPS on each tile
24: - Snapshot per camera or all three together (PNG, shared timestamp)
25: - Record all three at once (one MP4/WebM per camera)
26: - Hot-plug: cameras reconnect when they're plugged back in
27: 
28: ## Recording robot tasks — `record.py`
29: 
30: ```bash
31: ./record.py --task pick_cube              # starts recording immediately (preview window + hotkeys)
32: ./record.py --task pick_cube --idle       # preview first, press SPACE to start each trial
33: ./record.py --task pick_cube --save-raw   # also save each camera unprocessed (for datasets)
34: ./record.py --list                        # show detected cameras / assignment
35: ./record.py -h                            # all options
36: ```
37: On the first run `uv` installs `opencv-python` + `numpy` (inline script deps). Needs `ffmpeg` (Homebrew).
38: 
39: The recorder reads all 3 cameras directly (FaceTime is never opened) and builds the same view as the
40: frontend. It can run while the browser frontend is open.
41: Output is a 1920×1080 H.264 MP4 per clip, with a burned-in timestamp, the task/clip name and the frame number.
42: 
43: **Hotkeys** (in the preview window or the terminal):
44: 
45: | Key | Action |
46: |---|---|
47: | `SPACE` | start / pause / resume |
48: | `n` | next clip (finish current, start a new one) |
49: | `y` / `x` | label clip **success** / **fail** and finish it (SPACE starts the next trial) |
50: | `e` | end clip without a label |
51: | `m` | add a marker (e.g. "grasp", "release") |
52: | `s` | snapshot PNG (composite + each raw camera) |
53: | `+` / `-` | output FPS (5–30). A recording clip continues in a new linked clip after 1 s |
54: | `c` | color mode: normal, grayscale, high-contrast (CLAHE), warm, cool, invert |
55: | `[` `]` / `;` `'` | brightness / contrast, `0` resets |
56: | `l` / `f` | layout: grid (with clock/info panel), row, focus, single / which camera gets focus |
57: | `1` `2` `3` | hide / show wrist, RealSense, Logitech |
58: | `t` | timestamp overlay on/off |
59: | `h` | help overlay · `q` / `ESC` / Ctrl+C stops and saves |
60: 
61: **Output** — `recordings/<date>_<task>/`:
62: - `clip001.mp4`: the composite video
63: - `clip001_<cam>.mp4`: one per camera, only with `--save-raw`
64: - `clip001_frames.csv`: per-frame wall-clock time, plus each camera's frame number and frame age in ms. Use it to sync with robot logs.
65: - `clip001.json`: outcome, markers, pauses, setting changes, and the dropped/duplicated frame counts
66: - `session.json`: every clip with its outcome and success/fail totals. The success rate also prints when you quit.
67: 
68: Pauses are cut out of the video. Video time always equals recorded time: if the loop falls behind, a frame is repeated, and the json counts it.
69: 
70: **Screen mode** (literally screen-records the web frontend):
71: `./record.py --source screen --crop chrome` finds the Chrome tab at `localhost:8770`, brings it forward
72: and records that window area. Your terminal needs Screen Recording permission. It records
73: **whatever is on top of that area** (other windows, popups), so camera mode is preferred for clean footage.
74: 
75: ## Notes
76: - The D415 RGB sensor comes through as a normal UVC webcam. Depth and IR need `pyrealsense2` / librealsense and can't be read in a browser.
77: - With three USB cameras on one hub, 1080p@30 on every camera can run out of USB bandwidth. If a tile fails to open, drop to 720p or 480p, or move cameras to separate ports.
